page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 series, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a nominal base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores via hyperthreading, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI) alongside standard AES and integer bit manipulation instructions.

System memory is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, adhering to the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of general enterprise compute tiers. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage and is provisioned without bundled disks, requiring network-attached managed disks or Premium Storage for persistent operating system and data volumes. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results place the D16s_v4 squarely in the middle 50th percentile across most standard multi-core computing metrics, with a PassMark CPU score of 15,816.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,684.0. While its single-core stress-ng throughput registers in the lower 25th percentile at 1,412.09, large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 73.63 GB/sec and Redis SET performance clocks at 13.9 million operations per second. Light AI workloads via small 135M language models achieve 123.52 tokens per second for generation, though medium 7B model prompt processing drops to a weaker 24.58 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the D16s_v4 offers balanced cost efficiency for enterprise infrastructure that requires steady multi-threaded execution without paying for specialized GPU or high-speed local NVMe capacity. Because disk persistence depends entirely on external storage, users should account for remote storage latency when architecting I/O-heavy environments. The VM is suited for static web serving, enterprise application hosting, build systems, Redis caching, and mid-tier database deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure D16s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and VNNI extensions, this instance offers balanced compute and memory density without bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the middle tier for multi-threaded performance, demonstrating a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,684.0, a PassMark score of 15,816.41, and uncached read memory bandwidth of 73.63 GB/sec. Although single-core throughput under intensive stress tests is modest, its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides cost-effective infrastructure for Redis caching tiers, web application servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and relational database workloads backed by remote Azure Premium Storage.
